data.text: Checking which test, if any, covers the placeholder-crate ownership scenario.
The other scenarios hold. Only the placeholder-crate ownership scenario has no test. Writing the findings file now.

Nine of the ten scenarios hold. One fails: no test checks the rust-workspace scenario "Placeholder crate ownership" (`no_test`). I wrote that single finding to `openspec/changes/232-rust-link-gates/.run/validator/findings.json`. As instructed, I ran no build, test or git command, so all of this comes from reading the code and tests.

**The failing scenario.** The ownership mapping is in the delta spec's source comment, so the code side is there. But no test checks that the 14 placeholder crate globs (`crates/kernel/vcs/**`, `crates/apps/cli/**` and the rest) map to rust-workspace:
- `link_gates_corpus.rs` only fails on `complete-capabilities`, `live-references` and `tagged-functions`. It leaves out `owned-once`.
- No TypeScript test checks ownership across the repository.

Other Code ownership scenarios in the repo have no direct tests either. If you treat these scenarios as declared by the spec rather than tested, you can drop this finding.

**Scenarios that hold:**
- **Rust ADRs are accepted:** `tests/rust-adrs.test.ts` and `decisions/024-rust-link-enforcement.md` both list the two new checks. The test would fail on the base code.
- **Items of the tags fixture** and **Nodes of the link graph fixture:** the new Function column is asserted for every row. The base code had no `function` field, so these tests would not compile there.
- **The three link gates fixture scenarios** (the findings, another group, the manifest error): I checked each expected finding's line number, rule order and message against the fixture files and `gates/*.rs`, and they match.
- **The three change fixture scenarios:** the base findings match, and so do the single `sum` finding with `001-totals` and the case where `002-missing` doesn't exist.
- **Repository passes the link gates:** `link_gates_corpus.rs` exists and uses `OSQ_CHANGE` when it is set. It is marked `#[ignore]`, so it only runs when ignored tests are included. The executor's results file says it passes with `OSQ_CHANGE` set.
